newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares dive 2.52 pct in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares dive 2.52 pct in thin trade.

text.p: Istanbul shares extended morning losses in afternoon selling on Thursday amid fresh political concerns which also depressed trade volume, brokers said.

The IMKB National-100 closed at 1,471, down 38 points, or 2.52 percent from Wednesday, following a 1.26 percent morning drop. Trade volume shrank to 11.01 trillion lira ($79.6 million) from Wednesday's 15.35 trillion ($111.2 million).
Brokers said the market began to wait for next week's two important meetings to be attended by top military generals and Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan.
They added that news about a top prosecutor calling on the constitutional court to outlaw Erbakan's Welfare Party (RP) for threatening the secularist state also began to annoy the market.

"The legal challenge to close the RP and the military meetings due end-month produced negative expectations and affected the market. But the index is holding on with strong support awaited between 1,400 and 1,440," said Ibrahim Musul from Sahin securities.

The Supreme Military Council meeting held twice a year to discuss promotions, retirements and disciplionary issues in the army is due on May 26 and the monthly National Security Council (NSC) meeting on May 31.
The NSC had urged Erbakan's Islamist-led coalition government to take tough measures against rising Islamist activism at its February meeting. It is expected to repeat its demands next week.
The government has been ailing since the February NSC meeting. Parliament voted in favour of dropping a censure motion against the government on Tuesday.
"Political uncertainty again dominates the market. I expect direction to become more clear next week," said Hasan Soydan from Garanti securities.
